t: Pemulwuy raids around Parramatta
c: Indigenous Australians led by Pemulwuy also conducted raids around Parramatta during the period between 1795 and 1802.

t: Mounted Police deployed to upper Hunter Region
c: Later they were deployed to the upper Hunter Region in 1826 after fighting broke out there between Wonnarua and Kamilaroi people and settlers.

t: War on Liverpool Plains between British and Indigenous
c: War took place across the Liverpool Plains, with 16 British and up to 500 Indigenous Australians being killed between 1832 and 1838.

t: Aboriginal resistance kills over 50 British
c: Over 50 British were killed between 1828 and 1830 in what was the "most successful Aboriginal resistance in Australia's history".

t: Lieutenant-Governor Arthur offensive in Black War
c: In 1830 Lieutenant-Governor Arthur attempted to end the "Black War" through a massive offensive.

t: First British settlement in Western Australia established
c: The first British settlement in Western Australia was established by a detachment of soldiers at Albany in 1826.

t: Yagan arrested and sentenced to death
c: In 1832 Yagan and two others were arrested and sentenced to death, but settler Robert Menli Lyon argued that Yagan was defending his land from invasion and…

t: Gold discovery sparks prospectors onto Wangkathaa land
c: The discovery of gold near Coolgardie in 1892 brought thousands of prospectors onto Wangkathaa land, causing sporadic fighting.

t: Governor Hindmarsh proclaims native treatment policy
c: On the initial Proclamation Day in 1836 Governor Hindmarsh, made a brief statement that explicitly stated how the native population should be treated.

t: Battle of Broken River
c: A clash at Benalla in 1838 known as the Battle of Broken River of which at least seven white settlers were killed, marked the beginning of the frontier…

t: Raymond Evans calculates Queensland Native Police casualties
c: In 2009 professor Raymond Evans calculated the Indigenous fatalities caused by the Queensland Native Police Force alone as no less than 24,000.

t: Queensland Native Police Force formed under Frederick Walker
c: Queensland's Native Police Force was formed by the Government of New South Wales in 1848, under the well-connected Commandant Frederick Walker.

t: Fort Dundas established on Melville Island
c: The initial settlement at Fort Dundas on Melville Island was established in 1824 but was abandoned in 1829 due to attacks from the local Tiwi people.

t: Fighting near Fort Wellington, Cobourg Peninsula
c: Some fighting also took place near Fort Wellington on the Cobourg Peninsula between its establishment in 1827 and abandonment in 1829.

t: Fort Victoria established on Cobourg Peninsula
c: The third British settlement, Fort Victoria, was also established on the Cobourg Peninsula in 1838 but was abandoned in 1849.

t: Permanent settlement established at Darwin
c: A permanent settlement was established at modern-day Darwin in 1869 and attempts by pastoralists to occupy Indigenous land led to conflict.

t: Deas Thomson moves for federation committee
c: In 1857, Deas Thomson moved for a New South Wales Parliamentary Select Committee on the question of Australian federation.

t: Wentworth founds General Association for Australian Colonies

t: Henry Parkes proposes Federal Council
c: Sir Henry Parkes, then colonial secretary of New South Wales, first proposed a Federal Council body in 1867.

t: Parkes raises colonial federation issue as New South Wales premier

t: Australasian colonies hold informal federation meeting
c: An informal meeting attended by official representatives from the Australasian colonies was held in 1890.

t: Britain grants self-government to Australian colonies
c: In 1855 and 1856, Britain granted self-government to New South Wales, the new colony of Victoria, Van Diemen's Land (renamed Tasmania) and South Australia.

t: Anti-Chinese riots on Victorian goldfields
c: Anti-Chinese riots erupted on the Victorian goldfields in 1856 and in New South Wales in 1860.

t: Colonial constitutions gain Royal Assent
c: The constitutions for New South Wales, Victoria and Van Diemen's Land (renamed Tasmania in 1856) gained Royal Assent in 1855, that for South Australia in 1856.

t: Convict transportation to Western Australia ends
c: Transportation of convicts to Western Australia ended in 1868 and the colony was granted self-government in 1890.

t: Sheep and cattle grazing expand inland
c: The spread of sheep and cattle grazing after 1850 brought further conflict with Aboriginal tribes more distant from the closely settled areas.

t: Victorian Women's Suffrage Society formed in Victoria
c: Henrietta Dugdale, Annie Lowe, and Elizabeth Rennick formed the Victorian Women's Suffrage Society, the first suffrage society in Australia in 1884.

t: Women's suffrage societies formed in South Australia
c: Societies to promote women's suffrage were also formed in South Australia in 1888 and New South Wales in 1891.

t: Six missions established in Victoria
c: Six missions in Victoria were established by 1860.

t: Sisters of Charity open St Vincent's Hospital
c: The Sisters of Charity opened St Vincent's Hospital in Sydney in 1857.

t: Colonial governments withdraw funding from religious schools
c: Between 1872 and 1896 all colonial governments withdrew state funding of religious schools, and the Catholic church responded by expanding its school system as…

t: Salvation Army and Catholic missions established in Australia
c: The Salvation Army commenced in 1880 and Catholic parish missions such as the Redemptorists, Vincentians and Passionists were established.

t: New South Wales establishes school council

t: Clarke's novel serialised in newspapers
c: Marcus Clarke's For the Term of His Natural Life was serialised in 1870–72 before being published as a book in Melbourne and London a few years later.

t: Rolf Boldrewood's Robbery Under Arms serialised
Australian Rules Football begins
c: Australian Rules Football began in 1858 and quickly became popular in Victoria, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania.

t: First metropolitan Rugby Union competition in Sydney
c: The first metropolitan Rugby Union competition was organised in Sydney in 1874 and the sport became popular in New South Wales and Queensland.

t: Peter Lalor elected to Victorian Legislative Assembly
c: Rebel leader Peter Lalor was elected to the Victorian Legislative Assembly in 1856.

t: Poll tax on Chinese immigrants enacted
c: The legislative remedy came in the form of a poll tax, assented to on 12 June 1855, made payable by Chinese immigrants.

t: Universal adult male suffrage introduced

t: Committee formed for Eureka Stockade centenary
c: In 1954, a committee of Ballarat locals was formed to coordinate events to mark the centenary of the Eureka Stockade.

t: Eureka Flag displayed at Sovereign Hill
c: The Eureka Flag was temporarily on display at Sovereign Hill during 1987, while renovation work was being carried out at the Art Gallery of Ballarat.

t: Museum of Australian Democracy at Eureka relaunched
c: In 2013 it was relaunched as the Museum of Australian Democracy at Eureka with the aid of a further $5 million in funding from both the Australian and…

t: City of Ballarat assumes museum responsibility
c: In 2018, the City of Ballarat council resolved to assume responsibility for managing the facility.

t: Spencer Street Station redesignation announced
c: The Spencer Street Station redesignation was announced in December 2005.

t: New South Wales Legislative Council created
c: A legislative body, the New South Wales Legislative Council, was created in 1825, which was an appointed body whose function was to advise the Governor.

t: Postal voting introduced in Western Australia
c: A form of postal voting was introduced in Western Australia in 1877, followed by an improved method in South Australia in 1890.

t: Female suffrage granted in New South Wales
c: Female suffrage was granted in New South Wales in 1902, Tasmania in 1903, Queensland in 1905 and Victoria in 1908.

t: Commonwealth Franchise Act establishes uniform federal voting
c: In 1902, the Commonwealth Parliament passed the Commonwealth Franchise Act 1902, which established a uniform franchise law for the federal Parliament.

t: Northern Territory granted Legislative Council
c: In 1947, the territory was granted a Legislative Council with six elected members and seven members appointed by the Administrator for the Northern Territory.

t: Aboriginal Territorians granted voting rights
c: In 1962, all Aboriginal Territorians were granted the right to vote in territorial and federal elections.

t: Northern Territory establishes fully elected Legislative Assembly
c: In 1974, a fully elected Legislative Assembly was established and the Northern Territory had its first representative parliament.

t: Compulsory voting introduced federally
c: Compulsory voting was introduced at the federal level in 1924 (in 1984 for Aboriginal Australians), at the state level in Victoria in 1926, followed by NSW…

t: Queensland Elections Act excludes Aboriginal people from voting
c: Under the Queensland Elections Act (1885), no "aboriginal native of Australia, Asia, Africa, or the Islands of the Pacific" was entitled to vote.

t: Western Australia enfranchises Indigenous Australians
c: In 1962, Western Australia enfranchised Indigenous Australians and those of Asian, African or Pacific Islander descent.

t: Prisoners serving less than five years allowed to vote
c: In 1983, this disenfranchisement was relaxed and prisoners serving a sentence for a crime punishable under the law for less than 5 years were allowed to vote.

t: Prisoner voting rights limited to those serving five years or longer

t: City Bank of Sydney absorbed by Australian Bank of Commerce
c: The City Bank of Sydney (absorbed by the Australian Bank of Commerce in 1917) is noted as one that did not close its doors.

t: South Sea Islander labour repatriation announced from Queensland

t: High Court strikes down New Protection legislation
c: In 1908, the High Court of Australia struck down the New Protection legislation as unconstitutional in R v Barger.

t: Free Trade Party renamed Anti-Socialist Party
c: In 1906 the federal Free Trade Party changed its name to the Anti-Socialist Party to emphasize its pro-business policies.

t: Formal Australian administration of Northern Territory begins
Royal Australian Navy established
c: The Fisher Labor government increased the naval budget and in 1911 established the Royal Australian Navy.

t: Federation Drought breaks, economic growth follows
c: The breaking of the Federation Drought in 1903 heralded a period of strong economic growth.

t: Wave of strikes by miners and workers
c: Lower wages and perceptions of profiteering by some businesses led, in 1916, to a wave of strikes by miners, waterside workers and shearers.

t: Communist Party of Australia formed
c: Following the success of the Bolshevik Revolution in Russia the Communist Party of Australia was formed in 1920 and, though remaining electorally…

t: Labor Party wins landslide election victory
c: The Labor Party under James Scullin won the 1929 election in a landslide but was quite unable to cope with the Depression.

t: Labor loses power to United Australia Party led by Lyons

t: Robert Menzies succeeds Joseph Lyons as PM
c: Lyons died in 1939 and was succeeded by Robert Menzies.

t: Billy Hughes appointed Minister for External Affairs
c: Billy Hughes was brought back into cabinet by Lyons as Minister for External Affairs in 1937.

t: Hughes heads Australian Defence Force recruitment drive
c: From 1938, Lyons used Hughes to head a recruitment drive for the Australian Defence Force.

t: Prime Minister Lyons dies; Menzies succeeds him

t: Federal Capital Territory formed for future Canberra
c: The Federal Capital Territory (later renamed the Australian Capital Territory) was formed in 1911 as the location for the future federal capital of Canberra.

t: Melbourne becomes temporary seat of government
c: Melbourne was the temporary seat of government from 1901 to 1927 while Canberra was being constructed.

t: Church unification attempts fail
c: Attempts to unite the Congregationalist, Methodist, and Presbyterian churches failed in 1901–13 and again in 1917–25.

t: Australian Survey Office established
c: The Australian Survey Office was established in 1910.

t: Composer George Marshall-Hall migrates to Melbourne
c: George Marshall-Hall was a British composer who migrated to Melbourne in 1891 and whose opera Stella (1909) is set in colonial Australia.

t: Local record production begins in Australia
c: Local commercial record production began in 1926 and May Brahe's "Bless this House" (1927) became the most recorded Australian song.

t: Sixth Infantry Division partially formed in United Kingdom
c: A sixth infantry division, the 6th Division, was partially formed in the United Kingdom February 1917.
